children: Kimberly-Clark's third-quarter net sales were relatively flat year over year as favorable currency and Arbex Joint Venture supply-agreement sales were offset by lower organic sales. Net income attributable to the company rose, driven largely by a $1.4 billion after-tax gain on the IFP transaction; continuing-operations income also increased, reflecting lower tax expense.
¹ Reported as “Net Sales”. ² Reported as “Net Income Attributable to Kimberly-Clark Corporation”. ³ Reported as “Diluted Earnings per Share”.
: Decreased 1.3%, primarily driven by lower pricing; volumes declined 0.3%, including an approximately 270-basis-point China disruption headwind.
: Sales grew 0.9%; operating profit increased 2.7%, led by productivity savings and lower advertising spend.
: Sales fell 2.8% and operating profit declined 32.7%, primarily reflecting unfavorable pricing net of cost inflation and China disruption.
: Fell 110 basis points to 34.9%; unfavorable pricing net of cost inflation and supply-chain investments were partly offset by approximately $115 million of productivity savings.
: Completed November 2, 2026; the integration program is expected to result in approximately $3.1 billion of cumulative pre-tax charges through 2029.
